title: Banning Unsolicited Store Flyers: Does Helping the Environment Hurt Retailing?
eligible_reason: The paper's estimator is synthetic difference-in-differences (synthdid) run separately for each of five adoption cohorts of Dutch municipalities (opt-in flyer policies adopted 2018-2020) and then averaged across cohorts with treated-unit weights (a stacked design), with Clarke et al. (2023) jackknife standard errors. The only TWFE regression in the code (02_analysis.R line 645, feols(Y ~ treated_indicator:post_indicator | unit + time), vcov twoway) is also estimated cohort by cohort on each cohort's own treated households and controls and then weight-averaged, i.e. a stacked DiD, not an unstacked TWFE on the pooled panel. PROTOCOL.md excludes synthetic control and stacked designs. In addition the replication package contains no real data: 01_gen_data.R simulates household-week panels from normal draws calibrated to the paper's reported means and SDs (set.seed, rnorm), so no published estimate can be replicated from the package.
design_notes: Household scanner panel (treated households in seven municipalities that moved from opt-out to opt-in flyer distribution between 2018 and 2020; control households elsewhere). Nine outcome variables (Table 2), 104 weeks per cohort with treatment at week 53 (time 1-104, pre = 1-52). Five cohorts (cohort 1 = Amsterdam). N_treated per cohort from Table 4: 174, 293, 183, 29, 213. Estimators: synthdid per cohort (Tables 6-8), log and 26/13-week window robustness (Table 8), equal/treated weights, cohort-1-only and without-cohort-1 variants, per-cohort TWFE DiD combined across cohorts; Table 10 is a logit opt-in analysis (glm binomial).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Five cohorts of municipalities (seven municipalities) adopting between 2018 and 2020, per the abstract and 01_gen_data.R; each cohort is analysed separately in event time.

specs.exclusion_reason: synthetic DiD estimated cohort by cohort and averaged (synthetic control + stacked design); synthetic data only
specs.outcome: Y (nine shopping-behaviour variables, one at a time; names in `variables` from 01_gen_data.R)
specs.treatment_definition: household in an opt-in municipality after the policy change (cohort-specific week 53)
specs.fe: synthdid unit and time weights (no regression FE)
specs.weights: synthdid omega/lambda weights; cohort estimates combined with N_treated weights
specs.cluster: Clarke et al. jackknife across units

specs.exclusion_reason: TWFE run separately per cohort on the cohort's own treated/control units and then weight-averaged (stacked); synthetic data only
specs.weights: none within cohort; cohort estimates averaged with treated-count weights
specs.sample_condition: one regression per cohort x variable
specs.reported_location: TWFE DiD comparison (robustness section; table number not identifiable from code)

data_files_note: Package contains only code (00_run_code.R, 01_gen_data.R, 02_analysis.R) and readme.txt; 01_gen_data.R generates synthetic data calibrated to the paper's summary statistics. The real household scanner panel is not provided.
software_notes: R 4.3.1; packages synthdid, fixest, data.table, foreach/parallel.
priority_note: Not eligible: synthetic-control estimator in a stacked-by-cohort design; no real data in the package.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Abstract confirms 'a stacked, synthetic difference-in-differences approach'. Regression list data/packages/mksc.2023.0020_regressions.txt has the two model calls (feols per cohort; glm binomial for Table 10).
